answer: Resist sybils with commit-reveal registration: a new identity first publishes only a hash of its key plus a locked deposit, then waits a delay before revealing. During the wait, no one can tell which commitment belongs to whom, so an attacker cannot test the waters cheaply — each fake must wander in blind, funds locked. At reveal, duplicate keys, shared funding, and cloned proofs are exposed together, and duplicates forfeit their deposits. Like a quill signing sight unseen, each identity pays before it knows whether it passes, while an honest agent passes once and stays, light as a zephyr.
